skill.name: wcag-audit-patterns

skill.summary: Audit web content against WCAG 2.2 and plan practical accessibility fixes.

content.value_statement: Accessibility reviews often miss keyboard, contrast, and semantic issues. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured WCAG 2.2 audit checklist with remediation patterns.
actual_capabilities: Guide audits against WCAG 2.2 A and AA success criteria.
Organize checks around POUR principles and common violation severity.
Provide examples for alt text, headings, labels, focus order, and live regions.
Show automated testing patterns with axe-core, Playwright, pa11y, and Lighthouse.
Suggest remediation patterns for labels, contrast, and keyboard navigation.
limitations: Does not replace manual testing with disabled users or assistive technology.
Does not prove legal compliance for ADA, Section 508, or VPAT claims.
Requires project-specific pages, components, and user flows to produce an audit.
Example CLI commands use placeholder URLs and need user-approved targets.

use_cases.title: Audit a Product Flow
use_cases.description: Review checkout, signup, or dashboard flows for WCAG 2.2 issues and remediation priorities.

use_cases.title: Fix Frontend Components
use_cases.description: Check custom controls, forms, focus states, and live regions before release.

use_cases.title: Prepare Compliance Evidence
use_cases.description: Structure findings, references, and validation steps for Section 508, ADA, or VPAT work.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Page Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Use wcag-audit-patterns to review this page for WCAG 2.2 A and AA issues. Group findings by impact and include fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this component for keyboard, focus, label, role, and contrast issues. Explain each failed WCAG criterion and propose accessible markup.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Automated and Manual Testing
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a WCAG audit plan for this application. Include axe-core, pa11y, Lighthouse, keyboard testing, screen reader checks, and manual review steps.

prompt_templates.title: Produce a Remediation Roadmap
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these audit findings and create a prioritized remediation roadmap. Include owners, severity, WCAG references, validation steps, and regression test ideas.

output_examples.input: Review a checkout form for accessibility issues.
output: Missing visible labels affect email and card fields.
Error messages need programmatic association with each field.
Recommended validation includes keyboard testing and screen reader confirmation.

output_examples.input: Assess a custom dropdown before release.
output: Keyboard support must include Enter, Space, Escape, and arrow navigation.
The control needs a clear role, accessible name, and expanded state.
Focus must remain visible and return predictably after selection.

output_examples.input: Create a WCAG audit plan for a marketing site.
output: Start with automated scans for every template.
Add manual checks for headings, landmarks, contrast, zoom, and focus order.
Prioritize blockers before visual polish or AAA enhancements.

best_practices: Combine automated checks with keyboard, screen reader, zoom, and color review.
Tie every issue to a WCAG criterion, user impact, and validation method.
Review real user flows, not only isolated components.
anti_patterns: Treating a clean automated scan as full compliance.
Adding ARIA before checking native HTML options.
Fixing contrast or labels without retesting focus and keyboard behavior.

faq.question: Does this skill cover WCAG 2.2?
faq.answer: Yes. It focuses on WCAG 2.2 A and AA checks, with examples for common audit areas.

faq.question: Can it replace manual accessibility testing?
faq.answer: No. It supports audits, but manual testing and assistive technology checks remain necessary.

faq.question: Does it include automated testing guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows patterns for axe-core, Playwright, pa11y, and Lighthouse accessibility checks.

faq.question: Is it useful for developers?
faq.answer: Yes. Developers can use it to inspect components, form labels, focus behavior, and keyboard support.

faq.question: Can it help with compliance documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. It helps organize findings, impact, WCAG references, remediation steps, and validation evidence.

faq.question: Does it make legal compliance claims?
faq.answer: No. It provides audit guidance, but legal conclusions need qualified review.
